scope: Texas resources open regardless of immigration status (food banks, community health centers, WIC, emergency Medicaid, CHIP Perinatal, county hospital financial assistance), refugee resettlement agencies, and immigrant legal services

records.name: Emergency Medicaid
records.organization: Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC)
records.description_en: Emergency Medicaid can pay for care for a sudden, serious medical emergency. It is for people who cannot get regular Medicaid because of their immigration status.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Texas policy says people without acceptable immigration status who apply for Emergency Medicaid do not have to meet the citizenship or immigration status rules. They still have to meet the other Medicaid rules, such as income.
records.how_to_apply: Apply through Your Texas Benefits or ask the hospital's financial counselor or eligibility office for help. You can call 2-1-1 for help finding where to apply.
records.notes: Texas Works Handbook A-310: undocumented applicants for Emergency Medicaid do not have to meet citizenship status requirements; A-342 says SAVE verification is not followed for Emergency Medicaid applicants. Coverage is limited to emergency medical conditions. Income and other rules still apply. Do not give legal advice about public-charge or immigration effects; refer to an immigration legal provider.

records.name: CHIP Perinatal
records.organization: Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC)
records.description_en: CHIP Perinatal pays for care during pregnancy. It also covers two doctor visits within 60 days after the pregnancy ends.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For pregnant women in Texas who do not qualify for Medicaid and do not have other health insurance. Monthly family income must be at or below the state limit (for example, $2,687 for one person or $4,599 for a family of three).
records.how_to_apply: Apply online at Your Texas Benefits. You can also call 2-1-1 for help with the application.
records.cost: Free or low cost for people who qualify
records.notes: The HHSC page read this session did not state the immigration-status rules for CHIP Perinatal. Confirm status rules with HHSC or 2-1-1 before telling a client they qualify. Income thresholds shown are from the HHSC page and may change each year.

records.name: Texas WIC (Women, Infants, and Children)
records.organization: Texas Health and Human Services Commission / Texas WIC
records.description_en: WIC gives healthy food, nutrition help, and breastfeeding support. It serves pregnant women, new moms, and children under age 5.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For pregnant or breastfeeding women, women who gave birth in the last 6 months, and parents or guardians of children under 5 who live in Texas and meet the income limit. People on Medicaid, SNAP, or TANF already meet the income rule.
documents_needed: Proof of Medicaid, SNAP, or TANF (if you have it)
records.how_to_apply: Apply online at texaswic.org, call 800-942-3678, or visit a local WIC office. Bring the listed documents to your first appointment.
records.notes: Income limits on the source page: $2,461/month for 1 person, $3,337 for 2, $4,212 for 3 (gross). The Texas WIC page read this session did not state a citizenship or immigration requirement. Children who are U.S. citizens can qualify even if parents are not. Find local offices at office.texaswic.org. Breastfeeding hotline: (855) 550-6667 (24/7).

records.name: 2-1-1 Texas
records.organization: Texas Health and Human Services Commission / 2-1-1 Texas
records.description_en: 2-1-1 is a free help line. It connects people to local help for food, health care, housing, and other needs.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Anyone in Texas can call.
records.how_to_apply: Dial 2-1-1 or call (877) 541-7905. You can also chat online in English or Spanish at 211texas.org.
records.notes: Alternate number: (877) 541-7905. Useful for finding local food pantries and clinics that do not ask about immigration status.

records.name: TexasLawHelp.org Legal Help Directory
records.description_en: TexasLawHelp.org has free legal information, forms, and a directory of legal aid groups. You can search for free or low-cost legal help near you.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Anyone can use the website. Each legal aid group has its own rules.
records.how_to_apply: Go to texaslawhelp.org/directory and search for legal aid groups that serve your area.
records.notes: The homepage read this session did not show a dedicated immigration topic; use the directory to find providers. Warn clients about notario fraud: only licensed attorneys or DOJ-accredited representatives should give immigration legal advice.

records.name: RAICES Legal and Refugee Services
records.organization: RAICES (Refugee and Immigrant Center for Education and Legal Services)
records.description_en: RAICES gives immigration legal services and social services to immigrants and refugees. It has offices in five Texas cities.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For immigrants and refugees in Texas. Call to find out if they can take your case.
records.how_to_apply: Call 1-833-372-4237 (1-833-3-RAICES) to ask for help.
records.notes: Offices in San Antonio, Austin, Corpus Christi, Dallas-Fort Worth, and Houston; counties listed are the office metro counties, not a confirmed service-area list. Mailing address: P.O. Box 786100, San Antonio, TX 78278. Fees were not stated on the page read.

records.name: American Gateways Immigration Legal Services
records.description_en: American Gateways gives free or low-cost immigration legal help. This includes asylum, VAWA, T and U visas, green cards, citizenship, DACA renewals, and family petitions.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For immigrants, refugees, and survivors of persecution, torture, conflict, and human trafficking in Central Texas who meet income guidelines and case priorities.
records.how_to_apply: Call your nearest office for a phone legal screening. Austin screenings are the 2nd and 4th full weeks of each month, Mon-Thu 9 AM-5 PM; San Antonio and Waco screenings are Mon-Fri 8:30 AM-4:30 PM.
records.cost: Free or low cost for those who meet income guidelines
records.notes: Austin phone ext. 200. San Antonio office: 2300 W. Commerce St., Ste. 313, San Antonio, TX 78207, (210) 521-4768 ext. 232. Waco office: 2323 Columbus Ave., Ste. C, Waco, TX 76701, same San Antonio number ext. 232. Counties listed are office counties; the site says 'Central Texas' without an exact list. Capacity for new clients is limited. For removal proceedings at San Antonio Immigration Court: (210) 864-2917.

records.name: Tahirih Justice Center - Houston
records.description_en: Tahirih gives free, private legal help and case management to immigrant survivors of gender-based violence. This includes domestic violence, sexual assault, forced marriage, and human trafficking.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For immigrants who have experienced violence because of their gender.
records.how_to_apply: Call the Houston office at 713-496-0100 or email houston@tahirih.org. You can also call the main line at 1-866-575-0071, Mon-Fri 9 AM-5 PM.
records.notes: Walk-ins are not accepted. Street address not listed on pages read. National helpline: (866) 575-0071. Service area beyond Harris County not confirmed.

records.name: Human Rights Initiative of North Texas
records.organization: Human Rights Initiative of North Texas (HRI)
records.description_en: HRI gives free legal and social services to immigrants. It helps asylum seekers, survivors of domestic violence and crime, and abused or abandoned children.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Free for people who live in North Texas and have income at or below 150% of the federal poverty level. HRI cannot help people who are in immigration detention.
records.how_to_apply: Call 214-855-0520. Help is by appointment only.
records.hours: Mon-Thu 9:00 AM-12:00 PM and 1:00 PM-5:00 PM
records.notes: Source says 'North Texas' without an exact county list; Dallas is the office county. Not able to serve people in detention.

records.name: Immigration Legal Services
records.description_en: Catholic Charities Dallas helps with family visas, citizenship, DACA, green cards, help for crime and domestic violence survivors, and some deportation cases. It also helps refugees and asylees apply for green cards.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to immigrants in North Texas. Free help may be available if income is under 125% of the poverty level or you get public benefits.
records.how_to_apply: New clients can book a consultation (Tuesdays and Fridays) using the chatbot on the website, or call 866-223-7500.
records.cost: Consultation $50-$150 depending on service; free for those under 125% FPL or on public benefits
records.notes: Catholic Charities Dallas also runs Refugee Services (listed on its homepage). Exact service-area counties not listed on the page read.

records.name: Immigration Legal Services
records.description_en: Low-cost immigration legal help for family petitions, green card renewal, DACA renewals, citizenship, and asylum. Fees are much lower than a private attorney.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For immigrants in Central Texas. Call to ask if they can help with your case.
records.how_to_apply: Call 512-651-6125 and leave a voicemail with your name, contact information, and a short description of your situation.
records.hours: Austin office Mon-Fri by appointment only; Georgetown office Tue and Thu at Carver Center
records.cost: Consultation $60 (money order or credit card); fees 60-80% less than a private attorney
records.notes: Georgetown site: Carver Center, 1200 W 17th St, Georgetown, TX 78626. The organization serves 25 Central Texas counties overall, but the county list was not shown; counties here are office counties. Has a consultation backlog. New DACA applications not accepted (renewals only). Scam alert: they never ask for payment through WhatsApp, Venmo, Zelle, or Cash App.

records.name: Estrella del Paso Immigration Legal Services
records.organization: Estrella del Paso (formerly Diocesan Migrant and Refugee Services)
records.description_en: Estrella del Paso gives free immigration legal help, consultations, and community education. It serves immigrants in West Texas and New Mexico.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For migrants and refugees in West Texas and New Mexico.
records.how_to_apply: Call 915-532-3975 to ask for a consultation.
records.cost: Mostly free (99% of services free in 2025)
records.notes: Its Unaccompanied Children's Program closed after federal funding was withheld. Service area described as West Texas and New Mexico; exact counties not listed.

records.name: Las Americas Immigrant Advocacy Center
records.description_en: Las Americas gives legal help to low-income immigrants in the El Paso border area. Its website has free fact sheets on asylum, DACA, U visas, TPS, and citizenship.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For low-income immigrants in the borderlands region.
records.how_to_apply: Call (915) 544-5126 or visit the website to find local resources.
records.notes: Official site is las-americas.org (with a hyphen). The domain lasamericas.org without the hyphen is parked and unrelated. Cost and intake hours not listed on pages read.

records.name: Galveston-Houston Immigrant Representation Project (GHIRP)
records.description_en: GHIRP gives immigration legal help, including free citizenship help, legal consultations, deportation defense, and help for crime and trafficking survivors.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Free citizenship legal services are for eligible residents of Galveston and Harris Counties.
records.how_to_apply: Call (713) 561-3059 or toll-free 1-866-301-3901, email info@ghirp.org, or use the contact form on the website.
records.cost: Free citizenship services for eligible residents; other fees not stated
records.notes: Galveston office: 2228 Mechanic Street, Ste. 302, Galveston, TX 77550. Toll-free: (866) 301-3901.

records.name: Equal Justice Center Worker Rights Legal Services
records.description_en: Equal Justice Center helps low-wage workers get back unpaid wages and fight unfair treatment at work. It also helps young immigrants with DACA.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For low-income workers and families, regardless of immigration status.
records.how_to_apply: Call the Worker Rights hotline at (800) 853-4028.
records.notes: Austin office direct line: (512) 474-0007. Also has Houston and San Antonio offices (addresses not confirmed). Source explicitly says it serves people regardless of immigration status. Fee structure not stated.

records.name: Texas RioGrande Legal Aid (TRLA)
records.description_en: TRLA gives free civil legal help to eligible low-income people in 68 counties in central and southwest Texas.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For eligible low-income people who live in TRLA's service area. Use the service map on the website to check your county.
records.how_to_apply: Call intake at (956) 996-8752, Monday-Friday 8 AM-5 PM, or visit an office.
records.notes: Covers 68 counties in central and southwest Texas; the exact county list is on the TRLA ArcGIS service map (not captured here). The homepage read this session did not confirm immigration as a practice area, and federally funded legal aid may have limits on serving some non-citizens; confirm eligibility at intake.

records.name: International Rescue Committee (IRC) in Dallas
records.description_en: IRC Dallas helps refugees settle in. It offers help with housing and food in the first months, job placement, English classes, mental health support, and immigration legal services such as green cards and work permits.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For refugees, asylees, survivors of human trafficking and torture, and other immigrants.
records.how_to_apply: Call (214) 461-9781 to ask about services.
records.notes: Resettlement services are tied to federal eligibility (refugee, asylee, SIV, certain parolees, trafficking survivors). Service-area counties not listed. Cost is not stated on the page; resettlement services are generally free to eligible clients, but confirm fees for legal services.

records.name: International Rescue Committee (IRC) in Abilene
records.description_en: IRC Abilene helps refugees and other newcomers settle in. It offers case management, job training, English classes, immigration services, youth programs, and short-term financial help.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For refugees, asylees, survivors of human trafficking and torture, and other immigrants.
records.how_to_apply: Call (325) 675-5643 to ask about services.
records.notes: Taylor is the office county; exact service area not listed. Resettlement services depend on federal immigration category.

records.name: YMCA International Services
records.description_en: YMCA International Services helps refugees and other humanitarian immigrants in the Houston area start new lives.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Serves refugees, Cuban and Haitian parolees, human trafficking survivors, Special Immigrant Visa holders from Iraq and Afghanistan, asylees, detained immigrants, unaccompanied minors, and VAWA recipients.
records.how_to_apply: Visit the YMCA International Services pages on ymcahouston.org or contact the YMCA of Greater Houston.
records.notes: Phone and street address were not shown on the page read; do not guess. Currently serves refugees from Afghanistan, Syria, Burma, Somalia, Ukraine, Venezuela, and about 20 other countries.

records.name: Refugee Services
records.organization: Interfaith Ministries for Greater Houston (IM Houston)
records.description_en: IM Houston helps refugee families settle in Houston. Help can include airport pickup, school sign-up, English practice, and family mentoring.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For refugee families resettled in the Houston area.
records.how_to_apply: Call IM Houston at 713-533-4900.
records.notes: Page read describes volunteer roles supporting refugee families; eligibility details for clients were not stated. Main IM Houston number used.

records.name: Humanitarian Respite Center
records.organization: Catholic Charities of the Rio Grande Valley
records.description_en: The Respite Center gives rest, warm meals, showers, clean clothes, medicine, and supplies to people and families in need.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Serves men, women, children, and families in need in the Rio Grande Valley.
records.how_to_apply: Call (956) 800-4427 or go to the center.
records.notes: Hours not stated; call before going. Cost not explicitly stated but described as charitable relief.

records.name: Emergency Assistance Program
records.organization: Catholic Charities of the Rio Grande Valley
records.description_en: Helps with electric, water, and gas bills, and other emergency costs like transportation. It also offers medical vouchers, medical visits, and help with prescriptions for people without insurance.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people in the Rio Grande Valley facing a money emergency. The page does not list exact rules; call to ask.
records.how_to_apply: Call or visit the San Juan office (956) 702-4088 or the Brownsville office (956) 541-0220.
records.address: 700 North Virgen de San Juan Blvd
records.notes: Brownsville office: 955 West Price Road, Brownsville, TX 78520, (956) 541-0220. Eligibility, documents, and hours not stated on the page; counties listed are office counties.

records.name: Harris Health Financial Assistance (Charity Care)
records.description_en: Harris Health offers lower-cost care on a sliding scale for people who qualify by household income. It is not insurance.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people with household income up to 150% of the federal poverty level.
records.how_to_apply: Call the Eligibility Call Center at 713-566-6509. There is no fee to apply.
records.hours: Mon-Fri 8:00 AM-4:00 PM; fourth Friday 8:00 AM-2:00 PM
records.notes: Page read did not state an immigration-status requirement or residency rule; confirm with the call center. If anyone asks for payment to process an application, report to the Compliance Hotline (844) 565-0621.

records.name: Parkland Financial Assistance (PFA)
records.description_en: Parkland financial counselors help people without insurance or with high bills find help paying for care. Options include Parkland Financial Assistance and a self-pay charity discount.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people who are uninsured, underinsured, or facing money hardship. Programs are based on income, household size, and other rules.
records.how_to_apply: Call Patient Financial Services at 214-590-8831, or meet a financial counselor near the hospital or a Parkland community health center.
records.address: Parkland Tower Garage, 2021 Medical District Drive
records.cost: Discounted or free based on eligibility
records.notes: Translation available in 166 languages. Page read did not state residency or immigration-status rules; confirm with a financial counselor.

records.name: CareLink
records.description_en: CareLink is a financial assistance program that makes care at University Health more affordable. It is not health insurance.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For Bexar County residents with household income at or below 250% of the federal poverty level who do not have and do not qualify for health insurance.
records.how_to_apply: Fill out the CareLink enrollment application online, or call CareLink Member Services at 210-358-3350 to schedule an appointment.
records.notes: Spanish application: forms.uhstx.com/CLMemberApp-SP.html. Page read did not mention immigration status; confirm with Member Services.

records.name: CommUnityCare Health Centers
records.description_en: CommUnityCare runs clinics for primary care, children's care, dental, behavioral health, women's health, and HIV care in the Austin area.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Serves patients regardless of income, health insurance, or ability to pay.
records.how_to_apply: Call the Patient Navigation Center at 512-978-9015 or book online through MyChart. Call before your first visit to be screened for financial help.
records.notes: Bilingual agents and translation services available. Pages read did not state FQHC status or immigration-status policy explicitly; 'regardless of ... ability to pay' is from the source.

records.name: Centro de Salud Familiar La Fe
records.organization: Centro de Salud Familiar La Fe
records.description_en: La Fe is a large federally qualified health center in El Paso. It gives affordable health care for all ages.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to the El Paso community. Call to ask about costs if you have no insurance.
records.how_to_apply: Call (915) 534-7979 to make an appointment.
records.cost: Affordable; sliding fee details not stated on page
records.notes: Confirmed FQHC on its own site. Federally qualified health centers generally offer sliding-fee discounts; confirm immigration and documentation questions with the clinic.

records.name: Lone Star Family Health Center
records.description_en: Lone Star Family Health Center is a federally qualified health center with a sliding fee discount program. It has clinics in Conroe, Grangerland, Huntsville, Magnolia, Spring, and Willis.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to the community. The sliding fee discount lowers costs based on income.
records.how_to_apply: Call 936-539-4004 to make an appointment and ask about the sliding fee discount program.
records.notes: Counties inferred from clinic cities (Conroe, Magnolia, Willis, Grangerland, Spring are in Montgomery/Harris area; Huntsville is Walker). Immigration-status policy not stated on the page.

records.name: Legacy Community Health
records.description_en: Legacy has clinics across the Houston area for adult medicine, children's care, OB/GYN, dental, behavioral health, vision, pharmacy, and HIV/STD testing.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to the community, including people with Medicaid and people without insurance. Call to ask about costs.
records.how_to_apply: Call (832) 548-5000 to make an appointment.
records.notes: Clinics include Alief, Baytown, Beaumont, Deer Park, East End, Fifth Ward, Fort Bend, Montrose, Northline, Southwest, Third Ward, Pasadena, and Acres Homes. The homepage read did not state FQHC status, sliding fee, or immigration policy; confirm with the clinic.

records.name: Central Texas Food Bank - Find Food
records.description_en: The Central Texas Food Bank gives free food through local pantries, mobile pantries, and programs for kids and older adults. It also helps people apply for SNAP.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Anyone in need in the 21-county area. You do not have to show ID, proof of income, or citizenship to get food.
records.how_to_apply: Use the Find Food Now tool on the website to search by ZIP code, or call 2-1-1. Some sites ask you to fill out a short form about where you live and your need.
records.notes: Source states people are not required to show ID, proof of income, or citizenship to receive food. SNAP help: (855) 366-3401. Bring bags or a cart.

records.name: North Texas Food Bank - Get Help
records.description_en: The North Texas Food Bank gives food through about 500 partner pantries and mobile food distributions. It also helps people apply for SNAP.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people in need in the 12-county North Texas service area.
records.how_to_apply: Use the Find A Food Pantry locator or mobile distribution schedule on the website, or call 214-330-1396.
records.notes: County list from ntfb.org/about-us/ (Denton County no longer served). SNAP help: (214) 269-0906. ID/immigration rules not stated on page; individual pantries set their own intake rules.

records.name: Tarrant Area Food Bank - Find Food
records.description_en: Tarrant Area Food Bank gives food through partner pantries in Fort Worth and 13 nearby counties. It also offers SNAP help, a senior box program, and home delivery.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people in need in the Fort Worth area and surrounding North Texas counties.
records.how_to_apply: Use the Find Food map on the website to find a pantry, and call ahead to check hours. Or call 817-857-7100.
records.notes: Serves Fort Worth and 13 surrounding counties; full county list not captured, so only the counties of its three offices (Fort Worth, Denton, Weatherford) are listed. TAFB North: 306 N. Loop 288, Ste. 113, Denton, TX 76209. TAFB West: 112 Winners Circle, Weatherford, TX 76087. ID/immigration rules not stated.

records.name: El Pasoans Fighting Hunger Food Bank
records.organization: El Pasoans Fighting Hunger Food Bank
records.description_en: This food bank gives food through its Mercado and about 65 partner pantries. It also helps people apply for SNAP.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people in need in El Paso and the surrounding area.
records.how_to_apply: Use the find-food tool on the website, or call (915) 298-0353.
records.notes: Exact county list not shown; El Paso is the office county. ID/immigration rules not stated on the page.
